chapter: The Washingtonians, Bechet and drum style
title: Bechet, Tricky Sam and Bubber Miley jamming at the Kentucky Club
summary: Greer lists Washingtonians and describes nightly jam sessions with Bechet, Tricky Sam and Bubber Miley.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: All of them. The Washingtonians. You mean ended up in the band. Charlie Hughes. Tricky replaced him. He got sick and Bubba went to -- Bubba went to Europe on his own, that's when -- no.
No, Whetsol went. He was trumpet player. Went to Europe with Al Jolson,* and Bubba took his place and Tricky, and in a lot of years Bechet came down and played with us.
Of course, Toby went to join Noble Sissl&n in Paris, so we got Bechet. The Washingtonian.

Bechet and Tricky and Bubba, every night was a jam session. We play our stuff, but then for an added attraction all them musicians was coming and hang out there. Bechet would take napkin off the table and put it in his teeth and hide his hands under the keys and drive you crazy and Tricky would take a plunger, he had an old tomato can all bent up. He'd make it sound like a bass, drive you crazy. Bubba take two notes, set you wild. That was the highlight of the thing. Play anything.

But them cats were jamming and them ofays couldn't get over it. A guy, a trumpet player come up to Bubba and offered him $25.00 for his mouthpiece. "Bubba how you...?" man, it's the mouthpiece." Say "would you sell it!" "I don't know." I give you $25.00 for it. Only for you." The mouthpiece ain't cost but two or three dollars.
